meta.notes: Long-delayed plain speech after a life of indirect carriers. Says "Correct." Does not explain the conspiracy, the Hum, or himself.

threads.source: B24, section 4.5. A gloved woman leaving the roof, not the fall.

hv_1.line: Three-forty. Correct. I keep it by the time signal. You'll be the one who is reading Miss Quell's log.

choices.label: What did you see on the nineteenth of July?

hv_1s.line: You can stand there. It is a free pavement. I had a hand in that.

choices.label: What did you see on the nineteenth of July?

hv_2.line: I thought saying nothing would keep me out of it. About seven minutes past nine by my watch. In the lightning, a woman in pale gloves coming down the ladder to the top landing, something flat under her arm and a bag on her wrist. In at the one window on that landing. I sat across a table from Mae Kessler for an afternoon. I know the walk.

choices.label: Why were you on the stair?
She lay thirty feet from the foot of it. You didn't look down?

hv_3.line: I am on no one's. It has been very expensive.

hv_4.line: Air. I am not supposed to be in that house. That stretch of the wall has no window in it. I built a great many listening rooms and I know what a blank wall is worth.

hv_5.line: No. That is the question and that is the answer. I saw her leave. I saw no fall. I'll say that to anyone with a pencil.
